author: Sharjeel Hashmat
title: Dubai 2026 so far: what the official numbers show
description: Dubai residential sales value rose 11% in Q1 2026, then fell 33% in Q2 and 46% in Q3 against 2025. Here is where the money still went, from the Dubai Land Department's own records.
metaDescription: Dubai residential sales value rose 11% in Q1 2026, then fell 33% in Q2 and 46% in Q3 against 2025.

body.p: Dubai residential sales were worth AED 251.3 billion from January to September 2026, down 25% from AED 335.8 billion in the same nine months of 2025. The year started stronger than 2025 and then turned.
These are residential sales only: homes sold, by registration date, across every Dubai area. Mortgages, gifts, land and commercial deals are excluded.

The sharpest drop against last year came in Q3, but against the quarter before it the fall slowed: AED 68.4 billion in Q3 against AED 75.4 billion in Q2. Part of the gap with 2025 is that 2025 itself kept rising through Q3. Press reports link the change to regional uncertainty since late February 2026 (press-reported, not in the official data).

body.p: The two areas that grew are both almost entirely off-plan master plans. The established, mostly resale districts in the list all fell by more than a third.

body.h: What these numbers do not tell you

ul: **Value is not price.** Value is the number of deals times their size. A 46% fall in value does not mean prices fell 46%; it can come from fewer deals, smaller deals, or both.
**Registrations can arrive late.** These figures are as the records stood on 30 October 2026. Late registrations can still add to recent months.
**One quarter is one data point.** Nothing here predicts the next quarter.
Price a unit on recent transactions in its own building and unit type, not on a citywide total.
In an off-plan area, check the project's escrow status and the developer's delivery record before the headline growth.
In a resale area with falling value, ask how many comparable units sold and at what price per square foot.

body.p: High for the figures: every number is computed from the Dubai Land Department's transaction records. The cause of the slowdown is press-reported only and is not stated as fact.
